For re-rendered viewpoint shift with STALE extrinsics, forward-splat (extract-then-place) pipelines have no escape hatch: every pixel's features are unconditionally lifted and placed by the (wrong) analytic transform, and nothing downstream can re-weight them by content. Correct NEW extrinsics at test time fix only the analytic half. Because depth/features/opacity are extrinsic-independent and the splat is cheap and differentiable, test-time self-calibration becomes nearly free: cache the backbone/neck outputs once, then sweep or gradient-descend candidate extrinsic corrections through only the renderer (GaussianLSS.py:243-269 re-renders 11 pitch hypotheses from cached tensors; lift_to_3d_diff at :127-146 even exposes d(BEV)/d(lidar2img)). A robust design should expose exactly this interface — a differentiable geometry knob decoupled from the backbone — so stale-extrinsic viewpoint shift can be corrected at inference without retraining or re-running the image branch.

The probabilistic splat fixes LSS's hard-quantization brittleness but encodes ONLY depth uncertainty: covariance is the second moment of the depth distribution along the ray (GaussianLSS.py:120-123), so small calibration error still rigidly shifts means with no compensating spread perpendicular to the ray. Two cheap hardening moves: (i) inflate/augment the 3D covariance with a pose-uncertainty term (rotation jitter of the ray, the same math as the existing depth covariance) so BEV features degrade gracefully under miscalibration; (ii) condition the depth/opacity heads on calibration (ray map or K,E embedding) or canonicalize images to a virtual camera, because the unconditioned metric depth head is the one place training-rig geometry (camera height/pitch/FOV) is silently memorized — the failure mode that survives even when correct new extrinsics are supplied on a new platform. The repo's own ablations (extnoise: 3-deg random extrinsic rotation augmentation, transforms.py:176-194; calib: learned BEV scorer over analytic corrections) are exactly the augmentation-vs-test-time-correction baselines a benchmark should compare.

lessons: Keep calibration purely analytic and downstream of feature extraction. DFA3D-CARLA deliberately disables the depth head's learned calibration encoder (cam_channel=0), whose design — normalizing lidar2img by a FIXED training-set reference tensor (cam_param_ref.pth) plus per-camera learned embeddings — is exactly the pattern that breaks cross-platform transfer even when the NEW extrinsics are correct: the network would see out-of-distribution normalized calibration values. With the analytic-only design, correct new extrinsics propagate to sampling locations, depth gates, and masks automatically; the only stale parameters are camera-slot identity embeddings (cams_embeds) and learned BEV-grid priors.

Inject depth in the WEIGHT path as a projection-consistency gate, not in the value/placement path. Because depth_score multiplies attention weights at the analytically projected (u,v,d), a stale-extrinsic misprojection is doubly penalized — wrong pixel AND depth-disagreement suppression — so errors degrade toward missing evidence (recall loss) instead of the extract-then-place failure mode (CAPE/BEVDet/BEVDepth) where confidently-featured pixels are splatted to wrong BEV cells. For re-rendered viewpoint shift with stale extrinsics, a weight-path depth gate predicts BEVFormer-like EXT≈IMG behavior with an extra self-suppression term; for transfer with correct extrinsics it predicts near-free adaptation of the gate itself.

An image-only metric-depth head (absolute 2–58 m bins, no ray/intrinsic conditioning) hides a platform prior in its weights: per-pixel depth statistics depend on camera height, pitch, and focal length seen in training. Under re-rendered viewpoint shift the predicted distribution stays tied to the ORIGINAL viewpoint's appearance while the analytic d coordinate moves with whatever extrinsics are fed, so the consistency gate is only as good as depth-prediction transfer. A robust design should parameterize depth per-ray (conditioned on the analytically computed ray direction/camera height from CURRENT calibration, not learned embeddings of it) or supervise in a ground-relative frame, keeping the conditioning analytic so it re-derives at test time.
